items.text: Quantity of content ideas submitted per period — meets or exceeds the required minimum
items.kpiTitle: Quantity of content ideas submitted per period

items.text: Quality of ideas — topics are original, niche-appropriate, and audience-relevant
Research quality — content briefs include accurate, credible, and usable source materials
Trend awareness — topics reflect current niche trends, seasonal opportunities, and algorithm patterns
Title and hook quality — proposed titles and hooks are click-worthy and competitive
Timeliness — ideas and briefs submitted before the scriptwriting deadline without requiring chasing
Collaboration — communicates clearly with CM and scriptwriter; responds to feedback constructively
Script output — meets or exceeds the required number of completed scripts per period
Hook quality — opening hooks are strong, engaging, and retain viewer attention within the first 30 seconds
Script structure — clear narrative arc, logical flow, effective re-hooks, and a strong CTA
Tone and niche alignment — writing style matches the channel's voice and audience expectations
Factual accuracy — all claims are supported by cited sources; no misinformation or unverified statistics
Word count accuracy — scripts consistently hit the target length for the assigned video duration
Revision responsiveness — revisions completed accurately and within the agreed turnaround time
Collaboration — communicates clearly with Ideator, CM, and editor; accepts feedback professionally
Design quality — thumbnails are visually striking, professional, and click-optimised
Niche alignment — designs match the tone and visual style of the assigned channel
CTR performance — thumbnails produced during this period achieved competitive click-through rates (where data is available)
Technical compliance — all thumbnails delivered in correct specifications (1280x720px, correct format and file size)
A/B testing delivery — alternate versions submitted alongside every primary thumbnail without exception
Timeliness — thumbnails delivered before the upload deadline with no delays to the production pipeline
Revision responsiveness — corrections applied accurately and promptly following CM or QA feedback
Asset management — source files saved and stored correctly in the designated company folder
Edit quality — finished videos are well-paced, clean, and engaging; no technical errors or visual gaps
Audio quality — voiceover and background music are balanced correctly; no sync errors
B-roll accuracy — footage used accurately matches the narration; no irrelevant or mismatched visuals
Style guide compliance — channel's visual identity (fonts, colours, transitions, overlays) consistently applied
Map/graphic quality — custom map animations and motion graphics are accurate and professionally executed
Export specification compliance — final file delivered in correct resolution, format, and bitrate every time
Self-review quality — editor's own pre-submission checks catch errors before QA stage (fewer QA flags = better self-review)
Timeliness — edits submitted to QA by the agreed deadline within the content calendar
Revision quality — QA and CM feedback applied accurately and completely; no repeat errors after revision
Upload accuracy — videos uploaded to the correct channel with no wrong-channel errors
Metadata accuracy — titles, descriptions, and tags applied correctly and completely as provided
Thumbnail accuracy — correct thumbnail applied to every video; verified before submission
Schedule adherence — all videos uploaded on time as per the content calendar; no unexplained delays
Upload log maintenance — log kept up to date and submitted to CM on the agreed schedule
Error reporting — any upload failures, access issues, or YouTube policy flags reported immediately to the CM and Cenri/Flo
Credential compliance — platform credentials accessed only through the approved system; no sharing of access with unauthorised persons
Pipeline management — content calendar maintained and all production stages completed on schedule for every video in the period
Team coordination — assignments issued to all contractors with clear briefs, deadlines, and expectations; no preventable delays
Quality oversight — script, thumbnail, and video reviews completed before handoff; issues caught and corrected before reaching QA
Escalation handling — team concerns addressed at CM level appropriately; escalations to HR are well-documented and genuinely unresolvable at CM level
Channel performance — upload frequency and overall channel metrics (views, CTR, watch time) maintained or improved during the review period
Communication quality — responsive, clear, and professional in all team communications; issues addressed constructively not reactively
Upload package delivery — complete, labelled upload packages delivered to the Uploader with all required elements and no missing assets
Contractor development — proactively identifies team members who need support or recognition; raises concerns with HR in a timely manner
Review thoroughness — every video reviewed end-to-end; no errors missed that later appeared in published content
Review turnaround — QA reviews completed within the agreed timeframe; no delays to the upload schedule caused by QA
Feedback quality — feedback notes are specific, actionable, and clearly reference timestamps or sections; no vague comments
YouTube policy compliance — zero policy violations in published content that passed QA review during the period
Script and thumbnail review — scripts and thumbnails reviewed for accuracy and compliance before production proceeds
QA log maintenance — log updated after every review and submitted to the CM on the agreed schedule
Recurring issue reporting — patterns of repeated errors identified and escalated to the CM and Cenri for systemic improvement
Zero post-publish errors — no videos that passed QA required correction or were removed after publication due to a QA oversight
Handoff quality — the work they pass to you is complete, correctly labelled, and ready to use without rework
Reliability — hits agreed deadlines consistently; you rarely have to chase or wait on their part of the pipeline
Responsiveness — replies within working hours; you are not left blocked waiting for an answer
Clarity — briefs, notes, and messages are clear the first time; you do not have to ask twice to understand the task
Feedback handling — takes correction professionally and does not repeat the same issue after it has been raised
Accountability — flags their own mistakes and delays early rather than hiding them until they become your problem
Helpfulness — shares context and helps when asked, rather than working in a silo
Professionalism — respectful in group chats and calls; no blame-shifting, no drama, no venting about teammates
Brief clarity — you know what is expected of you without having to guess or ask repeatedly
Availability — reachable when you are blocked; does not leave you waiting on a decision
Feedback quality — specific and actionable, aimed at the work rather than the person
Fairness — workload, opportunities, and recognition are distributed fairly across the team
Decision-making — decides promptly instead of letting issues drift or escalate unnecessarily
Support and development — removes blockers and helps you improve at your role
Tone and respect — professional and constructive in all communication, especially under pressure
Follow-through — does what they said they would do, when they said they would do it
Confidence in their leadership — overall, you are glad to work under this lead
